newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH 1996 nine-month sales up 2.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: LVMH 1996 nine-month sales up 2.3 percent.

text.p: Sales of French flagship luxury goods maker LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton group rose 2.3 percent in the first nine months of 1996 from the same period last year, the company said on Tuesday.
The company said a positive customer reaction to its new perfumes would boost sales in the fourth quarter of the year.

"The favourable reception accorded the group's newest perfumes -- notably Champs Elysees at Guerlain and Organza at Givenchy -- will continue to have a favourable impact on sales during the fourth quarter of the year," the company said in a statement.
Total LVMH nine-month sales were 20.9 billion francs ($4.1 billion) in 1996, compared to 20.4 billion in 1995.
In the third quarter alone, LVMH sales wre up by six percent fuelled by a strong rebound in Louis Vuitton luggage and leather goods sales, which continued into October.
In the champagne segment, a three percent growth in the nine month sales volume went along with moderate retail price increases, while cognac sales rose by 12 percent.
In the luggage and leather goods segment, price adjustments and new store openings led to a "sharp" increase in sales.
In the perfume and beauty products segment, an effort to increase the selectivity of retailers continued to hit sales notably at Parfums Christian Dior.

The negative impact of currency fluctuations remained significant in the period, the statement added, since on a constant currency basis LVMH sales would have increased by 4.9 percent. -- Paris Newsroom 331 4221 5452. ($ = 5.056 French Francs)
